items.titleEn: Every WSL goal from the 2025/26 season
items.summaryEn: Look back on all 53 goals we scored in the WSL last season
bodyEn: Last season saw us record some memorable victories in the Women's Super League, with London derby successes and resounding wins over fierce rivals, and now you can watch every goal we scored in our league campaign.

We started as we meant to go on with a 4-1 win over London City, a game that saw Olivia Smith score one of our best goals of the season right at the start as she opened her Arsenal account with a stunner from 25 yards.

London derbies brought more success later in the season as Alessia Russo scored a memorable hat-trick against Spurs and Mariona Caldentey scored a beautiful goal to wrap up a 2-0 win over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.
Press play on the video at the top of the article to watch all 53 of our WSL goals from the 2025/26 season.

items.titleEn: The best of the boss at Villa Park with Bench Cam
items.summaryEn: Watch Mikel's reactions to Bukayo's goal, Ezri's debut and more
bodyEn: Bukayo Saka's second-half strike secured a 1-0 win at Villa Park on Monday night, and you can see how Mikel Arteta and his coaching staff reacted to the game with Bench Cam.
We extended our winning start to the season thanks to Bukayo's goal, making it three victories and three clean sheets from three games in 2026/27.

There were also first Premier League minutes in an Arsenal shirt for summer arrivals Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa, with the later making his Gunners debut against the side we signed him from last week.
To see how the boss and his staff reacted to these moments and the rest of the key highlights from Monday's game, press play on the video at the top of the article.

items.titleEn: Vote for your men's Player of the Month for August
items.summaryEn: Which one of Bukayo Saka, Riccardo Calafiori, Martin Odegaard or Gabriel gets your vote?
bodyEn: Voting is now open for our first Player of the Month poll of the 2026/27 season - but which of the four contenders will you opt for?

We kicked off the month by lifting the Community Shield with a 3-0 victory over Manchester City, before following that up with a 3-0 win over Coventry and 1-0 win at Aston Villa to ensure we started the season in perfect fashion.
Four contenders have been selected for the first prize of the campaign. Here are the candidates for you to choose from!
RICCARDO CALAFIORI
What a start to the season Riccardo Calafiori is having.
The full-back got our campaign off to the perfect start when he netted in the Community Shield against Manchester City in under 60 seconds.
Since then, Cala has helped us keep three clean sheets in a row as well as providing assists for Kai Havertz against Coventry and Bukayo Saka at Aston Villa.

August has proven to be a productive month for Cala since his move from Bologna, with his last five Premier League goal involvements for us having all been in the opening two games of the season in 25/26 and 26/27.
BUKAYO SAKA
Having ended the 25/26 strongly, Bukayo Saka has picked up where he left off.
After some positive minutes in the Community Shield triumph over Manchester City, Bukayo started and scored in our 3-0 victory over Coventry at Emirates Stadium.
Our English winger followed that up with the decisive goal in our 1-0 victory over Aston Villa at Villa Park to keep up perfect going into September.
KAI HAVERTZ
Martin Odegaard has led by example in August.
The skipper has started all three matches after a fantastic World Cup with Norway, showing his creative spark in our three successes.
Martin helped create our second goal against Manchester City in Cardiff, but before bagging one himself, he wrong-footed Gianluigi Donnarumma to slot into the corner.
Our captain then linked up well with Bukayo Saka and Ben White to net his first Premier League goal since December 2025 in our 3-0 opener against Coventry.
GABRIEL
Big Gabi marked six years as a Gunner on September 1, and he's once again showing why we brought him to Emirates Stadium back in 2020.
The Brazilian has slotted back into club life seamlessly this season, playing every minute in our first three outings.
In those three outings, we've kept three clean sheets to help pick up the first piece of silverware of the campaign plus two wins from two as Premier League reigning champions.
Which player gets your vote? Vote now!

items.titleEn: Tzolis answers fan questions in Ask Me Anything
items.summaryEn: Christos Tzolis recently took on a selection of supporter questions in our latest Ask Me Anything on Reddit!
bodyEn: Christos Tzolis recently took on a selection of supporter questions in our latest Ask Me Anything on Reddit!
He responded to queries about a footballer’s diet, the culture at Arsenal, and more.
Here’s what he had to say on the following subjects…

on rebounding from tough losses: I think losses are part of football and we know that's happening a lot and you have to only learn from the mistakes and know what you can do better the next time. So I think it's a good lesson sometimes to understand the loss. Of course, I don't like to lose, obviously, and everybody here doesn't like to lose, but sometimes they can make the team stick to each other better and improve small details. You don't have to detect it yourself. After a loss, step back and be ready for the next game.

on eating healthy and cheat meals:Actually, we really take care of our nutrition. My usual breakfast, I could say, is omelette with avocado, more or less, or sometimes porridge because I want to change the breakfast. Cheat meals... maybe after the game I can have a cheat meal. I like some sweets after the game. Maybe I can have a brownie or something like this. But nothing crazy. It's important to eat healthy.

on when he knew he was a first-team level talent:It's a nice question. I think around 12 or 13 years old, I knew I was quite good for my age. I was scoring a lot of goals in Greece. Obviously, back then, my target was to play for the first team of PAOK. That happened at the early age of 18, I did my debut. So more or less 13 or 14 years old I knew I could be a first team level player.

on the biggest change in terms of culture at Arsenal:I think it's such a big difference in how big Arsenal is because it's a worldwide team and it's one of the biggest teams in the world. It's crazy how many supporters are coming, even in the hotel, in the stadium and outside when we are on the bus. It's a big difference from my previous clubs. And how well it's organised, the club, in the training ground, the stadium and everything. I think it's top level and that makes the team also very big in terms of that. I think that's the most big difference I had.

on how much our players motivate each other to be better:Actually, everyone tries to help each other in training, on the pitch, during the games as well. We are one team that wants to improve and the aim is to win every time, so the standards are high in training as well. I can say the more experienced guys, they speak a lot, like Mikel Merino, Gabriel Magalhaes, Declan Rice, I can hear a lot - Myles as well. I think it's good to have these kind of players next to you and to learn from them.

on joining us after winning the Premier League:It's such an unbelievable feeling to sign for Arsenal, especially after the team won the Premier League last season. That makes it even more special to start the season with the champions. Actually I felt immediately like at home. They were very good with me. They were very welcoming and I settled in very good. That's thanks to my teammates and the staff members. I can see a very healthy dressing room over here.

on who would win a game between our left-footed and right-footed players:Who wins? That's a good question. We have a lot of left-footers also on the team. I believe the right-footers are going to win because we can use our left better as well. So we have the advantage to use both feet. So I'll go with the rights.

on the most unlikely bromance in the squad:I think Kai and Viktor. They are very close. That's nice to see because they play in the same position. Both are very good guys and they are good friends. Also, Viktor is only here one year and Kai has more years. So I didn't expect that they are going to be so close when I signed here.

on which teammate would be best at surviving on a remote island:That's difficult to say, because I'm only one month here, to know the skills of every player. But I would go with someone creative. Maybe I'd go with Martin Odegaard. I think he has the patience and the survival skills.

items.titleEn: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
items.summaryEn: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summerBringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aaron

It is all change at Villa and, although a little trepidation is inevitable, a refresh was probably overdue. At the same time, Unai Emery did not want to lose so many key players and Villa’s manager has made clear there is no such thing as a transition season in his eyes. Villa have generated about £300m from the sales of nine players and brought in 10 at a cost of about £250m. Villa have lowered their wage bill and changed the profile of their squad. Zion Suzuki, Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, names on the lips of Villa’s rivals, are particularly exciting signings. Last summer there was concern Villa had gone stale and 12 months ago they ended up fretting on deadline day – Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho joined on loan – but there was no such chaos this time. Perhaps Bournemouth’s best business was keeping hold of their coveted key players, chiefly Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan, Alex Scott and Tyler Adams. Bournemouth rejected bids from Chelsea for Scott and stayed true to their plan of resisting offers to give Marco Rose the best chance of succeeding, with the club attempting to juggle European competition and the league for the first time. The arrival of the Portugal centre-back António Silva, 22, from Benfica looks a typically smart replacement for Marcos Senesi, 29. Kroupi’s freak foot injury, which will probably keep him out until November, may have proved a blessing in disguise in terms of retaining the 20-year-old. BF

Mamadou Sangaré has added quality in midfield since joining from Lens and looks the bargain of the summer. Callum Wilson has brought experience up front after signing on a free and Jaidon Anthony provides cover on the flanks after his £15m move from Burnley. Deadline day deals to bring in the exciting Nigeria forward Femi Azeez from Millwall and the Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés from Stuttgart made it 12 signings in another summer of transition, Azeez’s arrival being announced almost 12 hours after the window shut. The departures of Jan Paul van Hecke, Carlos Baleba and Carl Rushworth brought in more than £140m as the Brighton model continues to deliver big profits, although losing last season’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, to Chelsea for a mere £5m may be the biggest loss if the new striker Promise David cannot bring the goals. Xabi Alonso’s appointment as manager was the biggest signing of the summer. Chelsea have been sensible since turning to the Spaniard. Morgan Rogers has started well after joining for £117m. Maxence Lacroix adds power in defence, Marco Palestra versatility on the flanks. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson can raise standards in the dressing room. But there was the usual revolving door. Money was made on a host of outgoings. Marc Cucurella, one of the world’s best left-backs and sold to Real Madrid, looks a bigger loss than Enzo Fernández. However a worry is that Chelsea did not replace Fernández after selling him to Manchester City for £125m, their late £47m move for Monaco’s Lamine Camara collapsing at the last. JS

Coventry also sought to address their lack of Premier League experience with Taiwo Awoniyi and Ethan Pinnock. Coventry were the highest scorers in English football’s top four tiers last season but the step up means the pressure is on Awoniyi, never prolific for Nottingham Forest, Sidiki Cherif, a promising 19-year-old, and Ellis Simms to deliver before Haji Wright returns from injury. The new manager, Pierre Sage, will at least be pleased to have secured more defensive reinforcements after losing Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea, with the loanees Honest Ahanor and Axel Disasi adding much-needed depth. Palace also kept hold of Ismaïla Sarr – presuming he doesn’t join a club in Saudi Arabia before the Sunday deadline there – after rejecting an approach from Liverpool for the Senegal forward. EA

It was a window that revealed the extent of The Friedkin Group’s ambitions, the strength of the club’s finances after the move to a new stadium, the state of the relationship between the manager and chief executive and the expertise of the senior leadership team; and none of it was positive. The owners deserve some credit for listening to fans and halting the self-defeating sale of Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest but otherwise it was a modest window that descended into a shambles. The club’s best player was sold for a below-market fee, a move for Folarin Balogun collapsed and although the equally desperate search for a right-back ended with Ainsley Maitland-Niles signing, David Moyes was left with one striker and a smaller squad than he started the day with, despite repeatedly urging his employers to strengthen. Gonzalo García, César Palacios and Manuel Ángel followed Arbeloa from Real Madrid and Shea Charles is an exciting signing from Southampton. Some stalwarts have left. Raúl Jiménez joined Wolves and Harry Wilson went to Leeds. Fulham looked to strengthen. They secured the midfielder Hugo Larsson and centre-back David Affengruber on deadline day but missed out on another target, the right-back Andrei Ratiu. JS

“Think of us like a volcano,” said Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali, in early July. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.” Two months on the Ilicali has presided over 18 signings, investing more than £150m and his manager, Sergej Jakirovic, has choreographed two Premier League wins. The horizon looks infinitely brighter than in June, when the playoff winners sold two players for a combined £8.5m to avoid breaching English Football League spending rules and a near-certain six-point deduction. Hull, remember, spent last season under a two-window EFL transfer embargo. They have compensated for that this summer and, although time will tell whether all those new faces are compatible, reasons for optimism remain real. Not least because last season’s cult hero loanee forward Joe Gelhardt has signed permanently from Leeds. Louise Taylor

Arrivals such as Exequiel Palacios and Julio Enciso should have no business in the lower reaches, and the former Fulham pair Sasa Lukic and Issa Diop add crucial experience. Gary O’Neil can call upon enviable depth in midfield and speed on the flanks, where Abdul Fatawu and Daizen Maeda look sharp. But time will tell whether Ipswich strengthened their defence sufficiently for regular tests of the kind they failed at Old Trafford on Sunday. Nick Ames

The importance of the acquisition of the England goalkeeper James Trafford from Manchester City should not be underestimated. Trafford will almost certainly provide Leeds with a few more extra points – not to mention enhance their play courtesy of his stellar footwork. Just in front of him Tarik Muharemovic looks an outstanding defensive buy. Harry Wilson raises creativity levels and the attacking tone. LT

The final window of Richard Hughes’s spell as sporting director raised more questions over Liverpool’s direction under Fenway Sports Group, owners soon to be enriched by a £2bn investment from 1892 Holdings. The shift towards paying big money for big names continued with Bradley Barcola’s arrival from Paris Saint-Germain while Jérémy Jacquet and Victor Muñoz followed the older policy of developing young potential. Yet weaknesses remain at right back, defensive midfield and on the right wing, where Mohamed Salah’s exit was foreseen from December. Squad depth is lacking and a lot rests on the return to full fitness of Hugo Ekitiké, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni. AH

With Enzo Fernández’s deadline day signing for a British record-equalling £125m, Enzo Maresca can have zero complaints about a first window as Manchester City’s head coach. The No 8 follows two No 6s, in Elliot Anderson (£116m) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (£85m), and the wide players Allan Elias (£34m) and Iliman Ndiaye (£60m plus £5m) as major signings, the total spend on incomings about £457.5m. Factor in how City have generated about £281.8m in outgoings for a net spend of £175.7m, the divisions third-biggest of the window, and this sizable investment has to work - particularly the acquisition of Fernández. This was the window of the midfielder for Manchester United, with three recruited: Youri Tielemans (a No 8), Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba (No 6s). Yet missing was a left-back despite the targeting of Lewis Hall, and others, plus reinforcements for the rest of a creaking rearguard. The reason? A lack of money or, maybe, a reluctance to spend unless the finance was generated by transfers. Manuel Ugarte’s long-term injury (preventing his sale) and Joshua Zirkzee’s reluctance to move were factors. Will the specialist Luke Shaw, plus the stand-in options of Parick Dorgu (a wing-back/left forward), Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui (right-backs), Lizandro Martínez (centre-back) and Baleba prove adequate? JJ
Key ins: Carlos Baleba (Brighton, £70m), Andrey Santos (Chelsea, £50m), Youri Tielemans (Aston Villa, £35m)
Key outs: Rasmus Højlund (Napoli, £43.2m), Casemiro (Inter Miami, free)

Newcastle describe their transfer window as “transformative” and, with reinvention the name of the game on Tyneside, it is easy to see why. After selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães for a grand total not too far off £250m, they have signed eight – mainly young – players. Along the way the spine of a team now managed by Matthias Jaissle rather than Eddie Howe has been renewed and new cult heroes including the former Benfica right-back Amar Dedic and the former Manchester City midfielder Nico González are emerging. The deadline day arrival of the exciting 21-year-old Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille is regarded as quite a coup. Have Newcastle choreographed a triumph from a window that, at one point, looked potentially disastrous? LT

Key ins: Nico González (Manchester City, £52m), Matias Fernandez-Pardo (Lille, £51m), Bazoumana Touré (Hoffenheim, £43m), Aladji Bamba (Monaco, £30m), Amar Dedic (Benfica, £29.5m), Lukas Hornicek (Braga, £25.7m), Ewen Jaouen (Reims, £21.6m), Sean Steur (Ajax, £20m)
Key outs: Sandro Tonali (Tottenham, £92.5m), Bruno Guimarães (Arsenal, £75m), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona, £69.3m), Nick Woltemade (Juventus, loan), Kieran Trippier (Wolves, free)

Receiving £116m for Elliot Anderson was proof that among the chaos in recent years, Forest have carried out some smart recruitment. After appointing Oliver Glasner, the club worked to provide for his needs, splashing out on Ousmane Diomande, while Xaver Schalger was a sensible acquisition for free, as was Daniel Muñoz at £22m. A No 9 was the priority and it required a club record £45m to acquire the long-term target Liam Delap, who fits the bill perfectly. Whether not sourcing a direct replacement for Anderson will hurt them remains to be seen but at least they did not panic, making it a measured window where they were able to trim the squad. Will Unwin

After last summer’s 14 new faces this had been a bit of a conservative, almost slightly underwhelming, window. Or at least it was until Crystal Palace tried to hijack Sunderland’s agreement to sign the Lyon winger Malick Fofana and the two Premier League clubs engaged in an astonishing deadline day tug of war involving private jets from both sitting on the tarmac at Lyon airport and Fofana undergoing a medical in France unsure as to his destination until finally choosing Wearside. Arguably Sunderland’s biggest achievement was keeping last season’s star players. If persuading Granit Xhaka to stay rather than defect to Chelsea was vital, Régis Le Bris will be similarly delighted to have retained widely admired individuals of the calibre of Enzo Le Fée, Robin Roefs and Noah Sadiki. LT

Key outs: Eliezer Mayenda (Rennes, £17.1m)

A comprehensive reboot, from back to front, featuring a club record outlay for a window and one of the most lavish by any club ever. In the first summer window since the departure of the longstanding chair Daniel Levy, the hierarchy have backed Roberto De Zerbi in an attempt to put the trauma of last season behind them. All the new signings have Premier League experience and – apart from Mateus Fernandes and Sávio – are aged 25 or over. In other words, they ought to be ready to hit the ground running. The opening two matches did not go to plan. It will get better. Won’t it? David Hytner

items.summaryEn: Our goalkeeper has joined the League One club for the 2026/27 season
bodyEn: Tommy Setford has joined League One side Stevenage on loan for the 2026/27 season.
The talented 20-year-old has become a valued member of our goalkeeping unit in his two years at the club and played an important supporting role as we became Premier League champions last season.
He joined us from Ajax’s renowned academy in July 2024 and made his debut against Preston North End in the Carabao Cup three months later, keeping a clean sheet in a 3-0 victory.
Tommy made his FA Cup debut in February this year as a substitute for Kepa Arrizabalaga in our 4-0 win against Wigan Athletic.
The Netherlands-born goalkeeper qualifies to play for England and has represented the Young Lions at every age group from under-16s to under-21s.
As well as his senior appearances for Arsenal, Tommy has also played regular PL2 and UEFA Youth League games across the last two seasons.
We wish Tommy all the best for his time with Stevenage and look forward to seeing him continue to develop his talent this coming season.

Please only purchase a ticket if you are planning to attend the match, and it is recommended you explore travel and accommodation options as soon as possible. The personal details of all attendees will be printed on match tickets, with checks conducted by the Italian authorities. Our goal is to ensure that as many supporters as possible have the chance to attend this game safely.
Ticket Details
Details for all travelling supporters will be required for each seat when making a purchase. Every ticket will have the name of the individual ticket holder noted on it.

All information must be submitted within 24 hours of your booking. Any bookings that do not have the travelling supporter details submitted by this deadline, will not be fulfilled. Passport details will also be required for each seated client when making a booking.
Please note that tickets will be sent to the lead client for each booking. Tickets must be used by the member assigned to the booking and must not be handed over to another individual.

Once you have completed your booking, you will be required to enter the personal details of every ticket holder in the group, via this link which will be accessible one hour after your booking. All information must be entered correctly and once submitted, you will not be able to edit these details.

Tickets for this game will be issued in a PDF format that must be printed or scanned by mobile phone and will be fulfilled and sent to the lead client member. Please ensure that your email address details are up to date.

All tickets will be checked at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona against the personal identity of the holder by SSC Napoli. Supporters must supply their physical passports or photo ID for such checks, and copies or other forms of ID will not be accepted in any form. Any tickets found to not be in possession of the named holders will be refused entry and the membership/s assigned to the seats may be suspended as a result.

When attending away fixtures, please ensure that your match ticket is scanned. It is your responsibility to make sure that your ticket is scanned correctly at the turnstile, in order that we receive the data proving your attendance, which will ensure that you keep the away credit earned for the fixture.

If you do have access issues on the day of the game, please speak to a steward or seek advice from the hosting club’s ticket office before entering the ground to confirm that your match attendance is recorded.

We monitor away match attendance from access control data which is recorded at the hosting club’s ground. We receive this information directly from the hosting club and use the data to confirm attendance.
Please be aware that additional documentation will not be accepted to prove away match attendance, including photographs, receipts, travel or hotel bookings.

If you fail to scan your away match ticket, the data we receive will show that you did not attend the fixture, and the away match loyalty point that has been credited to your membership account will be removed for this game.

The club also reserves the right to implement further away point removals for repeated occurrences as set out under section 3.10 of the Arsenal Away Match Ticket Terms and Conditions Season 2026-2027.

items.titleEn: Ethan Nwaneri joins Borussia Dortmund on loan
items.summaryEn: Our attacker has joined the German side for the rest of the 2026/27 season
bodyEn: Ethan Nwaneri has joined Bundesliga side Borussia Dortmund on a season-long loan.
The 19-year-old Hale End graduate has been with us since the age of eight and signed his first professional contract in March 2024 when he turned 17.

Ethan had already made history by that point, having made his first-team debut as a substitute away to Brentford in September 2022. Aged just 15 years and 181 days old, he became the youngest player in Premier League history, while the appearance also made him our youngest-ever player in any competition.

A breakthrough 2024/25 campaign saw Ethan make 37 appearances in all competitions, including 26 in the Premier League and seven in the UEFA Champions League. He scored his first goals for the club in September 2024, netting twice in our 5-1 Carabao Cup win against Bolton Wanderers, before opening his Premier League account two months later in our 3-0 win over Nottingham Forest at Emirates Stadium.
Ethan spent the second half of last season on loan in the south of France with Marseille, making 11 appearances in all competitions with the Ligue 1 side.
An England youth international, Ethan has represented the Young Lions at every age group from Under-16 to Under-21 level, making 58 appearances and scoring 27 goals
We wish Ethan all the best during his valuable time with Borussia Dortmund and look forward to following his continued development.
The loan deal is subject to the completion of regulatory processes.

bodyEn: Aston Villa completed the signings of Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis on deadline day, with Unai Emery confident that the club’s radical summer overhaul has left Villa in position to replicate their recent success. Villa, who have lost both of their Premier League games this campaign, have qualified for the Champions League in two of the past three seasons and won their first major trophy in 30 years after lifting the Europa League.

The £47m arrival of the 18-year-old winger Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain and £25m deal for Harwood-Bellis from Southampton represented Villa’s ninth and 10th summer signings respectively. Villa had generated more than £300m from the sales of nine players, six of whom started the Europa League triumph in Istanbul in May: Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Emiliano Martínez all departed Villa Park in recent weeks, Rogers and Martinez joining Chelsea.

Watkins’s £50m exit to the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, after rejecting Villa’s offer of a new contract, led to Villa signing Nicolas Jackson for an initial £47.5m that could rise to a club-record £65m. Earlier in the window, Villa signed Johan Manzambi for a club-record £52m from Freiburg but the Switzerland midfielder is yet to make his debut as he continues his recovery from a knee injury he sustained at the World Cup.

After the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal on Monday, Emery struck an upbeat tone. “We are happy how we are closing the transfer window,” the Villa manager said. “We are not regretting anything and the players who are joining are players that should be enough to rebuild the team with the structure we want. I think we replaced the players as we planned.”

Zion Suzuki, a £30m arrival from Parma, made his Villa debut against Arsenal and Villa’s new No 1 accepts the task of replacing Martínez is a “good challenge”. “It was my priority to play games so that is why I made the decision and I played in Belgium for one year, in Parma for two years,” said the 24-year-old, who joined Villa after a move to PSG collapsed in the final stages.

“In the end I am here and playing for Villa. I just wanted to come here for this club. There are so many expectations. It is not easy to play after [Martínez] but I want to help the team and be like him.

“It was very important to play in Serie A for two years and now I am confident. I made good steps and now I am here to play for the club. I want to enjoy this moment and help the team. I am really looking forward to [playing in] the Champions League but before that I want a first Premier League win to get some momentum.”
Newcastle, meanwhile, concluded a “transformational” transfer window by securing the target that topped their shopping list in May with only hours of the transfer window remaining.

The £51m signing of the Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille on deadline day is regarded as a considerable coup and prompted boardroom celebration at the end of a turbulent summer. The 21-year-old is Newcastle’s eighth signing of a transfer window during which Eddie Howe was replaced as manager by Matthias Jaissle and three of the team’s biggest names – Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães – were sold for a total approaching £250m.

Ross Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director, kept in frequent contact with Fernandez-Pardo’s advisers. “Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way,” Wilson said. “Back in May he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him. Now at the end of the window he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United and we are excited to welcome him.”

Fernandez-Pardo’s elusive movement and ability to operate as a No 10, a No 9 or wide-left attacker explains why Newcastle were prepared to stay patient for his signature. “A lot of hours went into this one,” Wilson said. “But we’re clear on our identity and Matias has speed, intensity and work rate in abundance. We believe in his profile a great deal. Our fans will enjoy him and I know he will also enjoy our amazing St James’ Park atmosphere.”

Jaissle seemed equally delighted to have reinforced his frontline with a versatile attacker. “We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal,” said the German, who has made three key signings in the £39m Amar Dedic, the £52m Nico González and now Fernandez-Pardo since arriving on Tyneside in early August. “Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage and the ability to take players on. We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.”

The Belgian said: “I’m really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club. I spoke to the head coach and he really showed me how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my career progression it made complete sense to come; I didn’t hesitate at all. I can’t wait to start my wonderful adventure here.”
Nick Woltemade’s failure to fit into Jaissle’s high-intensity gameplans explains why the Germany forward, signed for £70m from Stuttgart last August, has joined Juventus on a year-long loan.

Elsewhere, Barcelona have confirmed that Gabriel Jesus has joined from Arsenal on a permanent basis for a fee that is thought to be €10m (£8.6m). The Brazil striker was in attendance for Barcelona’s 5-2 win against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night after a deal was struck over the weekend and he leaves north London as only the 12th player to win the Premier League title with two clubs, having also done so with Manchester City.
Harvey Elliott has also joined Valencia on loan from Liverpool while, across Merseyside, Beto has sealed a £15.5m move from Everton to Fiorentina.

items.summaryEn: Atlético say they will not allow Barcelona to buy Álvarez Jesus poised for Barça and Martinelli for Al-HilalArsenal are running out of time to persuade Julián Álvarez to join them from Atlético Madrid after agreeing to sell Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fábio Vieira in deals collectively worth more than £70m.Álvarez has his heart set on joining Barcelona despite Atlético’s insistence they will not sell to their La Liga rivals – he returned to training on Sunday after being left out of their squad for the win against Sevilla. Continue reading...
bodyEn: Arsenal are running out of time to persuade Julián Álvarez to join them from Atlético Madrid after agreeing to sell Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fábio Vieira in deals collectively worth more than £70m.

Álvarez has his heart set on joining Barcelona despite Atlético’s insistence they will not sell to their La Liga rivals – he returned to training on Sunday after being left out of their squad for the win against Sevilla.

Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, is understood to have spoken last week to Álvarez in an effort to persuade the former Manchester City forward to return to the Premier League and to have been informed the Argentina international wants only Barcelona.
Asked directly about Álvarez after victory at Aston Villa on Monday, Arteta replied: “I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.”

But Arsenal’s manager did confirm they are seeking reinforcements. “We are trying to improve the squad and until tomorrow night we are going to do that,” he said. “I have been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now.”

Barcelona have agreed an £8.6m deal to sign Jesus, who has entered the final year of his contract after falling down the pecking order behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres. The 29-year-old Brazilian was at Camp Nou to watch the 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday. The Barcelona manager, Hansi Flick, said: “He’s a top striker and of course for us very important, he can give us a lot of things and [I’m] very happy that he’s here.”
However, the Spanish champions would like to sign another attacker after selling Ferran Torres to Paris Saint-Germain and are said to have not given up on Álvarez.
The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?

Atlético have agreed a deal with Juventus for Jonathan David on an initial loan with an option to make the Canada forward’s move permanent next summer. But they are understood to be determined to keep Álvarez, who joined from City in 2024.

Arsenal remain hopeful that the 26‑year‑old could change his mind but are believed to be monitoring several other attacking options. Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye was among the players on their shortlist but Manchester City are in advanced talks over a £65m deal for the Senegal forward. Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea and failed in an ambitious attempt to sign Vinícius Júnior, the Brazil forward signing a contract extension at Real Madrid.

Arsenal have signed Christos Tzolis to replace Leandro Trossard on the left but Martinelli’s expected departure to Al-Hilal for a club‑record £56m sale would create a space in the squad, although Eberechi Eze is also capable of playing there.

Martinelli, who scored six times in the Champions League last season but only once in the Premier League, was due to have his medical on Monday after being left out of Arsenal’s squad against Coventry on the opening weekend. His fee surpasses the £40m Liverpool paid Arsenal for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.

items.titleZh: 阿森纳同意出售马丁内利和热苏斯后，试图吸引胡利安·阿尔瓦雷斯加盟
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳同意出售马丁内利、热苏斯和维埃拉，总价超7000万镑，但仍努力说服阿尔瓦雷斯加盟。
bodyZh: 阿森纳在同意以总价超过7000万英镑出售加布里埃尔·马丁内利、加布里埃尔·热苏斯和法比奥·维埃拉后，正试图说服胡利安·阿尔瓦雷斯从马德里竞技加盟，但时间所剩无几。
阿尔瓦雷斯一心想要加盟巴塞罗那，尽管马竞坚持不会将球员卖给西甲对手——他在周日回归训练，此前被排除在对阵塞维利亚获胜的大名单之外。
据悉，阿森纳主教练米克尔·阿尔特塔上周与阿尔瓦雷斯进行了交谈，试图说服这位前曼城前锋重返英超，但得到的回复是这位阿根廷国脚只想去巴塞罗那。
在周一客场击败阿斯顿维拉后，阿尔特塔被直接问及阿尔瓦雷斯时回答：“我不知道。这由高层决定。”
但阿森纳主帅确认球队正在寻求补强。“我们正在努力提升阵容，直到明天晚上之前都会这样做，”他说。“我24小时没有与外界联系，因为我觉得自己的精力和注意力必须放在比赛上，但现在我要重新投入到工作中。”
巴塞罗那已同意以860万英镑签下热苏斯，这位29岁的巴西前锋在落后于凯·哈弗茨和维克托·哲凯赖什之后，合同已进入最后一年。他周一在诺坎普观看了5-2战胜巴列卡诺的比赛。巴萨主帅汉斯·弗利克表示：“他是一名顶级前锋，对我们来说当然非常重要，他能给我们带来很多帮助，[我]很高兴他在这里。”
然而，在将费兰·托雷斯出售给巴黎圣日耳曼后，西甲冠军希望再签下一位攻击手，据称他们并未放弃引进阿尔瓦雷斯。
《卫报》的每日足球游戏“On the ball”现已在iOS和Android应用中上线。你能根据线索认出这位英超球星吗？
马德里竞技已与尤文图斯就乔纳森·大卫达成协议，先租借后买断，明年夏天可以选择将这位加拿大前锋的转会永久化。但据悉他们决心留住阿尔瓦雷斯，后者于2024年从曼城加盟。
阿森纳仍希望这位26岁的球员能改变主意，但据信他们正在关注其他几个进攻选项。埃弗顿的伊利曼·恩迪亚耶在他们候选名单上，但曼城正在就这位塞内加尔前锋进行6500万英镑的深入谈判。阿森纳错过了摩根·罗杰斯（切尔西），并在尝试签下维尼修斯·儒尼奥尔时失败，这位巴西边锋与皇马续约。
订阅《每日足球》
用《卫报》对足球世界的看法开启你的夜晚
在时事通讯推广之后
阿森纳已签下克里斯托斯·佐利斯来替代左路的莱安德罗·特罗萨德，但马丁内利预计将以5600万英镑（俱乐部纪录）转会至利雅得新月，这将为球队腾出一个位置，尽管埃贝雷奇·埃泽也能踢该位置。
马丁内利上赛季在欧冠中打入六球，但英超仅一球入账。他原本预计周一接受体检，此前在首轮对阵考文垂的大名单中被排除。他的转会费超过了2017年利物浦为亚历克斯·张伯伦支付的4000万英镑。
维埃拉看起来将加盟汉堡，他在上赛季被租借至那里，转会费为860万英镑。

items.titleEn: Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal: Premier League – as it happened
items.summaryEn: Bukayo Saka scored the only goal as the champions made it two wins from two and condemned Villa to consecutive defeatsThe teams are out! You know what everyone’s wearing. A reduced capacity of around 37,000 at Villa Park, with the North Stand closed for the season to facilitate its expansion. We’ll be off in a couple of minutes.Pre-match postbag. “Poor Villa. They were so great last year. Then management sells off the heart of their team. Today they will get embarrassed by the Gunners. What a present to their ever loyal fans” – Mary Waltz Continue reading...
bodyEn: … and so we wind down with a reminder that Ben Fisher’s report from Villa Park should be your next port of call. Thanks for reading this MBM!

… and now it’s Unai Emery’s turn to speak to Sky. “We lost … we compete well … against the winner last year … we are trying to rebuild the team … but a lot of positive things … how we compete … better with the ball … we didn’t create clear chances, but we didn’t concede clear chances … it is positive for the next matches … we had our chances to draw the match … to lose one match is always painful … but after we must try to get positive things … how we can get better … we can feel confidence because how we want to build the team is true … I think the squad we have now is how we planned and has the players we wanted … now we work … work, work, work.”

Mikel Arteta talks to Sky Sports. “I am really happy … a massive win … it’s a tough place to come … we deserved it … a great squad performance … the finishers came in and did a magnificent job … I loved a lot of things I saw from my team … I always trust my players … we have to be really proud tonight … I don’t know [about the potential signing of Julian Alvarez], that is for the people upstairs.”

The match-winner Bukayo Saka speaks to Sky Sports. “Very very tough game, I’ll be honest, yeah … it’s not easy coming here … they made it really really hard for us so it feels even better to come out with the win … they were compact … catching us offside a lot … we weren’t able to implement our attacking patterns like we did last week … we wanted to push for the second … we weren’t at our highest level with the ball tonight but without it we were incredible … all the boys put in a shift … that helps with a clean sheet.”

Then, after an awkward back and forth with Sky pundit Thierry Henry, who is disappointed that Saka has yet to put up a 15-goal-plus-15-assist season, a statement the player heroically lets slide, Saka is asked if he’s watched Chelsea yet this season.
“Yeah, I’ve seen them.” “What do you think?”[beat, smile] “We’ll see on Sunday.”
An entertaining, if slightly odd, interview.

Ben Fisher was at Villa Park tonight, and his verdict has landed. Here it is … but a reminder that this MBM isn’t pulling down the shutters yet, as we wait to hear from both managers. For potentially awkward browser-based situations such as this, the Guardian recommends the implementation of a two-tab system.

Post-match postbag. “Thank you Matt Emerson (min 90+5). We do seem to be immediately back in the days of angst, gritted teeth, shouting impolite words at the screen, and generally hating football in the last 10 minutes of a match with only a one-goal lead. For the Arsenal fan, nostalgia is exactly as it used to be” – Charles Antaki
“Arsenal fans have a song for occasions like this. What’s Basque for George Graham?” – Kári Tulinius

Arsenal went about their business in the non-nonsense style. They stayed together, they held firm, they remained patient, and when Eberechi Eze and Riccardo Calafiori combined down the inside-left channel for the one moment of true quality in tonight’s match, Bukayo Saka couldn’t miss the tap-in they’d teed up. They celebrate their win and head off to prepare for the visit of Chelsea on Sunday. Two wins out of two for the champions, just as it’s two defeats from two for Aston Villa, who have yet to muster an attempt on target this season, and have a lot of thinking and subsequent work to do. They’re off to Hull on Saturday for a game that … well, it’s way too early for a must-win, but Villa won’t appreciate the noises off if they fail to take anything from that one as well.
How does that song go again?

90 min +9: McGinn steps across Gabriel, who nicks him from behind. But there’s no free kick. Seconds later, McGinn barges into the defender, who topples over with an affronted look on his face. It nearly bubbles over, but there’s no time for any of that, because …

90 min +8: Eze crosses from the left, looking for Guimaraes, romping in from the right. Maatsen slides in, a scissor action, but catches ball rather than man, which is just as well. It would have been a clear penalty otherwise.
90 min +6: Maatsen clatters Saka out on the right touchline in the you-shall-not-pass style. Into the book he goes. Villa frustrated, Arsenal doing a good job of running down the clock.

90 min +5: McGinn clips Merino out on the right touchline. On a booking, the Villa captain wants to watch himself here. Nothing comes of the free kick. “Looks like the carefree, freewheeling Arsenal, released from the burden of not winning the title, has lasted one whole match,” observes the tinder-dry Matt Emerson, one eyebrow hoisted high.

90 min +3: Buendia and Wan-Bissaka apply pressure down the right, but Guimaraes muscles them both out of the road, before ushering the ball out for a goal kick. Then he celebrates as though he’d just scored the clincher.
90 min +2: It’s all Villa in terms of possession … but they can’t get anything going in the final third.
90 min: There will be eight additional minutes! There’s been a lot of substitutions and some hot VAR action, to be fair.

89 min: Suzuki races out of his goal to deal with a long ball down the middle. A powerful header clear. And this is as good a time as any for Ben Suenaga, of 50 min fame, to explain himself re Japanese superstars in the Premier League: “I know I bring shame by uttering the words but for once with Suzuki we can have a protagonist.”

88 min: How’s this for a stat, flashed up by Sky Sports? Aston Villa have yet to have a shot on target this season! Coventry next on the list with four attempts, while Palace, Leeds and Forest have had five.

86 min: Saka wins a corner down the right … then wastes it. McGinn tries to find Garnacho with a long pass … but overhits it. Raya claims, and waits an age with the ball at his feet before a Villa player closes him down. Abraham finally arrives, and as Raya picks up, both players have a short conversation. For a second, it threatens to escalate, but the two grown men eventually see sense. We play on.
85 min: Zubimendi comes on for Rice, who isn’t moving freely.
84 min: Maatsen scampers down the left and enters the box, going over as Rice and White sandwich him. He screams for a penalty, but there’s no way that’ll be given. And it isn’t.
83 min: Arsenal are sitting back, holding their shape. Villa seeing the majority of the ball for the first time this evening.

81 min: Now McGinn goes into the book for an agricultural lunge through the back of Merino. That wasn’t so great, and he’s lucky the referee has been, for the most part, in a laissez-faire mood tonight.
80 min: Alysson is booked for a late clip on Gabriel.

79 min: Mosquera is indeed unable to continue, so Konsa comes on for his Arsenal debut … and though there’s a few boos, the majority of home fans applaud their former player, who played such a big part in last season’s Europa League victory. That a lovely – and pretty cool – moment.
78 min: … but first, a couple of Villa debutants, as Garnacho and Wan-Bissaka come on for Barkley and Cash.
77 min: Mosquera goes down with what looks like cramp. Looks like a baptism of fire coming up for erstwhile Villa hero Konsa.

75 min: Suzuki makes good by saving from Havertz, the Arsenal striker having been put clean through by Guimaraes. Havertz opened his body and looked for the bottom left, but the keeper won the duel with a fine parry.

74 min: Havertz has a dig from the edge of the box. Suzuki spills the shot, which rebounds the best part of ten yards in front of him, but there’s nobody in 1979 yellow to take advantage, and he covers the ground to gather.
73 min: Alysson immediately gets involved, tearing his way past Calafiori down the right. He’s unable to find anyone in the centre with his low cross. His aim not so true.
72 min: … so Aston Villa respond by throwing on Abraham and Alysson, at the expense of Jackson and Hemmings.
70 min: Arsenal send on Merino and Guimarães in place of Lewis-Skelly and Odegaard …

68 min: Odegaard finds Havertz in space inside the box on the right. He’s tugged back by Kamara, but neither ref nor VAR shows any interest in giving a spot kick. Then Villa go up the other end, Maatsen nibbled at by White as he cuts into the box from the left, but ref and VAR collectively shrug again. Just about everyone in the crowd fuming, for one reason or another.

66 min: Hemmings strides into a pocket of space down the middle of the park. He’s got Barkley to his right, but tries to release Jackson down the middle with a slide-rule pass. Rice is on point to intercept with a swagger.

65 min: … and so having said that, Villa finally reach the Arsenal box, McGinn embarking on a baroque ramble down the inside-right channel. But he can’t get a shot away, and when he cuts back for Cash, Calafiori is on point to deal with the danger.
63 min: … and as if to prove that point, Arsenal slip straight back into a state of calm authority. Villa are yet to respond.

61 min: That goal had sort of been coming. On Sky, Gary Neville points out that Arsenal hadn’t really looked like scoring, but were in the ascendency and staying patient, and finally got their reward.

That little chain of events had put Villa fans in a good humour. But they’re not so happy now. Gabriel finds Eze to the left of the box. Eze plays Calafiori in down the channel. Calafiori slides ahead of Lindelof to meet the pass and whip it low into the centre, and Saka, beating his old foe Maatsen, can’t miss from a couple of yards.
57 min: Odegaard whips a cheeky free kick over the wall and inches wide of the right-hand post. Suzuki hadn’t been expecting it, and wouldn’t have got there. Goal kick.
56 min: VAR gets involved. Maatsen did foul Saka, leaning into his back … but the foul occurred just outside the box, to the right of the D. It’ll be a free kick to Arsenal instead.

54 min: Maatsen’s woes continue as Saka nips in ahead of him down the right, and he leans in from behind, bringing the winger down as he enters the box. After some thought, the referee points to the spot.

52 min: Thinking about that, Ben … Shinji Kagawa (Manchester United), Shinji Okazaki (Leicester City), Takumi Minamino and Wataru Endo (both Liverpool), Japanese Premier League title-winners all, may want a word.

50 min: Rice curls a delicious cross in from the right, but Havertz can’t beat Lindelof in the air at the far stick. Suzuki claims. Speaking of whom … “Here is hoping Japan have our first Premier League superstar in Zion!” begins Ben Suenaga. “Quite a jump coming from Parma but he is looking right at home. No disrespect to Mitoma and Daizen.”
48 min: Maatsen looks for Jackson this time, with a pass down the left touchline, but only manages to roll the ball out of play, nowhere near his team-mate. Not the best 60 seconds of his career.

47 min: Barkley spots Maatsen in acres of space out on the left. He loops a pass down the flank. Maatsen enters the box and, with only Jackson in the middle, and not in that much space, opts for the spectacular, aiming for the top-left corner. He finds the top-left corner of the Holte End.
Aston Villa get the second half underway. Arsenal have hooked Tzolis, who was on a booking and involved in a running duel with Cash, and replaced him with Eze.

Half-time postbag II, because why not? “Football refereeing is so stuck in the subjective age and so little reference is made to the actual stated rulebook that there will no improvement in consistency or ‘fairness’. Listen to the TV refs in rugby and cricket and they quote the rulebook and say whether what has happened does or does not comply with the factual rule. VAR in football is just the pundit class pontificating about this or that with little or no reference to any particular rule. I don’t like VAR for what it does tot he flow of the game, but being applied this badly just rankles with my sense of decency” – Nic

“Judging by his delivery to camera in the kit video, a career in the movies beckons for John McGinn after his playing days are over. He’s got the cheeky chappie Scot ex-footballer with a twinkle in his eye parts sewn up” – Simon McMahon

Half-time postbag. “I know the new stand will benefit Villa in the long term, but it feels like another thing counting against them at the moment: they could really use the extra support after the summer they’ve had. Always had a soft spot for Villa and hope they do well, but feel like this season could turn into a real struggle for them. Like a flirting with relegation-type struggle. Hope I’m wrong” – Joshua Keeling

“Emery is a splendid coach and a Villa legend, but this enforced rebuild needs to work and it needs to work fast. I am excited by Suzuki and Manzambi but Gomes, Goretzka, Wan-Bissaka, Jackson and Garnacho have bigger question marks than I’d like, and I’d have much rather been adding them to the squad for options than relying on them to hit the ground running. Plenty of Villa fans say ‘In Unai we trust…’ but… I’m trepidatious. Fingers crossed we can get a decent result tonight to build my confidence, and that of the squad!” – Benjamin Gravestock
“Arsenal fans must be delighted that Aston Villa have now taken on the mantle of encouraging us to Visit Rwanda” – Gary Byrne
A half that started promisingly but petered out a bit. The xG of 0.09 to 0.34 sounds about right, and tells most of the story.
45 min: There will be one of your additional first-half minutes.
43 min: Jackson skins Gabriel down the right and makes it as far as the box, but his low cross evades Hemmings at the near post.

41 min: A ball sent into the Villa box from the left. Torres leans into Calafiori, arm on back, and the Arsenal man goes over. He wants a penalty, but neither referee nor VAR shows any interest in awarding one, presumably citing the Not Enough In It For Me law that doesn’t exist but is so beloved of the pundit class. It’s a foul, though, isn’t it, no matter how soft? But here we are.

39 min: Cash clatters into the back of Tzolis, who wants more punishment meted out than the free kick that’s awarded. The referee’s not interested in booking Cash, and once the free kick is wasted, Tzolis gets dog’s abuse the next time he touches the ball.
37 min: Arsenal have enjoyed 73 percent of possession over the last ten minutes. They’ve not done too much with it.

35 min: White takes an age over a throw. It’s 12 seconds before the referee tells him to get a wriggle on, and 15 before it’s eventually taken. Villa not happy; they want the ball turned over to them. The referees have obviously tired of the new laws already. Good old PGMOL, or whatever they’ve been rebranded as this time.

33 min: Buendia crosses from the left. Jackson can’t meet it ahead of Raya, who claims. That move was started by another flawless Suzuki long pass, creamed down the right channel this time towards McGinn. The Japan keeper, excellent at the World Cup, looks the business.

31 min: Kamara skittles Lewis-Skelly 40 yards out. Odegaard loops the free kick into a crowded box. A game of head tennis breaks out before Villa clear. Arsenal’s set pieces haven’t been up to their usual standard. So far.
items.author: Scott Murray
items.titleZh: 阿斯顿维拉 0-1 阿森纳：英超联赛——比赛实录
items.summaryZh: 萨卡打入唯一进球，卫冕冠军取得两连胜，维拉遭遇两连败。
bodyZh: ……比赛即将结束，提醒您接下来可以阅读本·费舍尔从维拉公园发回的报道。感谢您阅读本场比赛的实时博客！

……现在轮到乌奈·埃梅里接受天空体育采访。“我们输了……我们拼得很好……面对去年的冠军……我们正在重建球队……但有很多积极的东西……我们如何拼搏……控球更好……我们没有创造出明确的机会，但也没有给对手明确的机会……这对接下来的比赛是积极的……我们有机会扳平比分……输球总是痛苦的……但之后我们必须尝试找到积极的东西……我们如何变得更好……我们能够感受到信心，因为我们想要打造球队的方式是真实的……我认为我们现在的阵容正是我们计划中的，拥有我们想要的球员……现在我们工作……工作，工作，工作。”
米克尔·阿尔特塔接受天空体育采访。“我非常高兴……这是一场重要的胜利……这是一个艰难的客场……我们配得上胜利……全队表现出色……替补上场的球员们做得非常好……我热爱我从球队身上看到的很多东西……我一直信任我的球员……今晚我们真的应该感到自豪……我不知道（关于可能签下胡利安·阿尔瓦雷斯的事），那是高层的事。”
进球功臣布卡约·萨卡接受天空体育采访。“非常非常艰难的比赛，说实话，是的……来这里不容易……他们给我们制造了很大的困难，所以最终赢球感觉更好……他们阵型紧凑……多次让我们越位……我们没能像上周那样实施进攻套路……我们想再进一球……今晚我们控球时不在最佳状态，但无球时我们表现不可思议……所有球员都付出了努力……这有助于保持零封。”
然后，在与天空体育评论员蒂埃里·亨利的尴尬对话中——亨利对萨卡尚未交出15球加15助攻的赛季感到失望，而萨卡大度地让这句话过去了——萨卡被问到这个赛季是否看过切尔西的比赛。
“是的，我看过他们。”“你觉得怎么样？”（停顿，微笑）“我们周日见。”
一场有趣但略奇怪的采访。
本·费舍尔今晚在维拉公园现场，他的报道已经出炉。在这里……但提醒您，本实时博客还没有结束，因为我们在等待两位主教练的发言。对于这种可能尴尬的浏览器情况，卫报建议使用双标签页系统。
赛后邮件。“感谢马特·埃默森（第90+5分钟）。我们似乎立刻回到了焦虑、咬紧牙关、对着屏幕喊粗话的时代，并且在比赛最后10分钟只领先一球时普遍讨厌足球。对于阿森纳球迷来说，怀旧正是如此。”——查尔斯·安塔基
“阿森纳球迷在这种场合有一首歌。乔治·格雷厄姆用巴斯克语怎么说？”——卡里·图利纽斯

阿森纳以严肃认真的风格完成了比赛。他们团结一致，稳固防守，保持耐心，当埃贝雷奇·埃泽和里卡尔多·卡拉菲奥里在左肋部配合创造出今晚唯一一次真正的机会时，布卡约·萨卡没有错过他们喂到嘴边的轻松推射。他们庆祝胜利，然后准备周日迎战切尔西。卫冕冠军两战两胜，而阿斯顿维拉则两战两败，本赛季至今还没有一次射正，他们有很多需要思考和随后要做的工作。他们周六将前往赫尔城进行一场……好吧，说必须赢还太早，但如果他们再拿不到任何分数，维拉不会喜欢那些噪音。
那首歌怎么唱来着？
第90+9分钟：麦金跨步挡住加布里埃尔，后者从背后碰了他一下。但没有任意球。几秒钟后，麦金撞向防守球员，后者带着被冒犯的表情倒地。冲突几乎爆发，但没有时间了，因为……
第90+8分钟：埃泽左路传中，找从右路冲进来的吉马良斯。马特森滑铲，剪刀脚，但碰到了球而不是人，这正好。否则那将是一个明显的点球。
第90+6分钟：马特森在右路边线处撞倒萨卡，方式如同“你不得通过”。他被出示黄牌。维拉感到沮丧，阿森纳在很好地消耗时间。
第90+5分钟：麦金在右路边线绊倒梅里诺。由于已有一张黄牌，维拉队长需要小心。任意球没有造成威胁。“看起来那支无忧无虑、自由奔放的阿森纳，摆脱了不夺冠的负担，持续了整整一场比赛，”干燥的马特·埃默森观察道，眉毛高高挑起。
第90+3分钟：布恩迪亚和万-比萨卡在右路施压，但吉马良斯将两人挤出路线，然后将球护出底线形成球门球。然后他庆祝得好像刚打进制胜球。
第90+2分钟：维拉在控球上占据绝对优势……但他们无法在进攻三区有所作为。
第90分钟：将补时8分钟！公平地说，比赛中有很多换人，还有一些热门的VAR争议。
第89分钟：铃木冲出球门处理中路的长传。一个有力的头球解围。现在是本·末永（第50分钟提到）解释关于日本球星在英超的好时机：“我知道说出这些话让我蒙羞，但这一次，有了铃木，我们终于可以有一个主角了。”
第88分钟：天空体育打出的这个数据如何？阿斯顿维拉本赛季还没有一次射正！考文垂以四次射正紧随其后，而水晶宫、利兹和森林有五次。
第86分钟：萨卡在右路赢得角球……然后浪费了机会。麦金试图长传找加纳乔……但传大了。拉亚拿到球，持球等待了很长时间，直到维拉球员逼上来。亚伯拉罕终于赶到，当拉亚捡起球时，两人简短交谈。一度有升级的迹象，但两个成年人最终恢复了理智。我们继续比赛。
第85分钟：苏维门迪换下赖斯，后者移动不太自如。
第84分钟：马特森沿左路快速推进进入禁区，在赖斯和怀特的夹击下倒地。他大声要点球，但那个球不可能判，也没有判。
第83分钟：阿森纳后撤保持阵型。维拉今晚第一次占据控球优势。
第81分钟：麦金因背后粗野铲倒梅里诺被黄牌警告。那动作不太好，而且他幸运的是裁判今晚总体上持放任态度。
第80分钟：阿利松因迟到铲倒加布里埃尔被黄牌警告。
第79分钟：莫斯克拉确实无法继续，因此孔萨替补登场，完成他在阿森纳的首秀……尽管有一些嘘声，但大多数主场球迷为这位前球员鼓掌，他在上赛季欧联杯夺冠中发挥了重要作用。那是一个可爱且相当酷的时刻。
第78分钟：……但首先，维拉两位新援登场，加纳乔和万-比萨卡替换巴克利和卡什。
第77分钟：莫斯克拉似乎抽筋倒地。看起来前维拉英雄孔萨即将迎来严峻考验。
第75分钟：铃木扑出了哈弗茨的射门，阿森纳前锋被吉马良斯直塞形成单刀。哈弗茨打开身体瞄准左下角，但门将精彩扑救赢得了对决。
第74分钟：哈弗茨禁区边缘射门。铃木脱手，球在他面前弹了十码远，但没有穿1979年黄色球衣的球员接应，他迅速起身将球抱住。
第73分钟：阿利松立即参与比赛，他沿右路突破卡拉菲奥里。他的低传未能找到中路的任何人。传球精度不够。
第72分钟：……因此阿斯顿维拉用亚伯拉罕和阿利松换下杰克逊和赫明斯。
第70分钟：阿森纳用梅里诺和吉马良斯换下刘易斯-斯凯利和厄德高……
第68分钟：厄德高在禁区右侧找到空位的哈弗茨。他被卡马拉拉拽，但裁判和VAR都没有兴趣判罚点球。然后维拉进攻到另一侧，马特森从左路切入禁区时被怀特轻轻拉扯，但裁判和VAR再次集体耸肩。现场几乎所有人都因某种原因而愤怒。
第66分钟：赫明斯大步带球进入中路的空当。他右侧有巴克利，但试图用精准传球把球传给中路的杰克逊。赖斯适时拦截，显得非常自信。
第65分钟：……说到这个，维拉终于到达阿森纳禁区，麦金在右肋部进行了一次华丽的盘带。但他无法起脚射门，当他回传给卡什时，卡拉菲奥里及时处理了危险。
第63分钟：……仿佛为了证明这一点，阿森纳立刻回归平静掌控的状态。维拉还没有回应。
第61分钟：这个进球可以说是迟早的事。天空体育的加里·内维尔指出，阿森纳之前看起来并没有真正接近进球，但他们占据优势并保持耐心，最终得到了回报。
这一连串事件一度让维拉球迷心情不错。但他们现在不高兴了。加布里埃尔在禁区左侧找到埃泽。埃泽将球传入通道给卡拉菲奥里。卡拉菲奥里抢在林德洛夫之前滑铲接到传球，低平球扫到中路，萨卡击败老对手马特森，在几码处轻松推射空门。
第57分钟：厄德高踢出一记巧妙的任意球，越过人墙，稍稍偏出右门柱。铃木没有预料到，即使扑也够不到。球门球。
第56分钟：VAR介入。马特森确实对萨卡犯规，他倚靠了对方后背……但犯规发生在禁区外，位于弧顶右侧。阿森纳将获得任意球。
第54分钟：马特森的噩梦继续，萨卡在右路抢先一步，他从背后倚靠，将边锋放倒在禁区内。裁判思考后指向点球点。
第52分钟：想想这个，本……香川真司（曼联）、冈崎慎司（莱斯特城）、南野拓实和远藤航（利物浦），都是日本英超冠军得主，可能有话要说。
第50分钟：赖斯从右侧传出一记美妙的传中，但哈弗茨在远门柱未能争过林德洛夫。铃木拿到球。说到他……“希望日本拥有我们的第一位英超巨星——锡安！”本·末永开始说道。“从帕尔马来到英超是个不小的跳跃，但他看起来非常适应。没有对三笘薰和守田英正不敬。”
第48分钟：马特森这次传球找杰克逊，沿着左路边线传球，但只是将球滚出界外，离队友很远。这不是他职业生涯最好的60秒。
第47分钟：巴克利看到马特森在左路有巨大空当。他将球传到边路。马特森进入禁区，中路只有杰克逊，而且空间不大，他选择了出人意料的方式，瞄准左上角。他打中了霍尔蒂看台的左上角。
阿斯顿维拉开始下半场比赛。阿森纳换下了佐利斯，他吃到一张黄牌，并且与卡什有持续对抗，埃泽替换了他。
中场邮件之二，为什么不呢？“足球裁判太主观了，很少参考实际规则手册，因此在一致性和‘公平性’上不会有改进。听听橄榄球和板球比赛的电视裁判，他们会引用规则手册，并说明所发生的事是否符合事实规则。足球中的VAR只是解说员就这或那发表意见，很少参考具体规则。我不喜欢VAR对比赛节奏的影响，但应用得这么糟糕，确实冒犯了我的正义感。”——尼克
“从他在球衣视频中对镜头的表现来看，约翰·麦金退役后演艺事业在向他招手。他那种眼神闪烁的顽皮苏格兰前足球运动员的角色已经预订了。”——西蒙·麦克马洪
中场邮件。“我知道新看台对维拉长期有利，但感觉这是目前对他们不利的另一件事：在经历了这样一个夏天后，他们真的需要额外的支持。我一直对维拉有好感，希望他们能表现出色，但感觉这个赛季他们可能会陷入真正的挣扎。有点像保级边缘的挣扎。希望我错了。”——约书亚·基林
“埃梅里是一位出色的教练，也是维拉传奇，但这次被迫重建必须成功，而且必须快速成功。我对铃木和曼赞比感到兴奋，但戈梅斯、戈雷茨卡、万-比萨卡、杰克逊和加纳乔身上的问号比我想要的要多，我宁愿他们是阵容中的选择，而不是指望他们一鸣惊人。很多维拉球迷说‘我们信任乌奈……’，但我感到忐忑。祈祷我们今晚能有个好结果，以增强我和球队的信心！”——本杰明·格雷夫斯托克
“阿森纳球迷一定很高兴阿斯顿维拉现在承担了邀请我们‘访问卢旺达’的角色。”——加里·伯恩
上半场开局不错，但后来有点平淡。预期进球0.09对0.34听起来差不多，说明了大部分问题。
第45分钟：上半场将补时1分钟。
第43分钟：杰克逊在右路摆脱加布里埃尔，进入禁区，但他的低传在近门柱错过了赫明斯。
第41分钟：一记传球进入维拉禁区。托雷斯靠在卡拉菲奥里身上，手臂压背，阿森纳球员倒地。他想要点球，但裁判和VAR都没有兴趣判罚，可能援引了“对我来说够不着”法则，这条法则不存在但解说界很钟爱。但这确实是个犯规，不是吗，无论多轻？但我们就在这。
第39分钟：卡什撞倒佐利斯后背，佐利斯希望得到比任意球更严厉的处罚。裁判无意对卡什出牌，一旦任意球浪费，佐利斯下次触球就遭到球迷谩骂。
第37分钟：阿森纳在过去十分钟内拥有73%的控球率。他们并没有做出太多文章。
第35分钟：怀特在掷界外球时拖延时间。12秒后裁判才催他快发，15秒后界外球才最终掷出。维拉不满；他们希望得到球权。裁判显然已经厌倦了新规则。真是优秀的PGMOL，或者不管他们这次改名成什么。
第33分钟：布恩迪亚左侧传中。杰克逊没能抢在拉亚之前碰到球，拉亚接住。那次进攻是由铃木又一次完美长传发起的，这次是向右路传给麦金。这位在世界杯上表现出色的日本门将看起来很有实力。
第31分钟：卡马拉在40码处撞倒刘易斯-斯凯利。厄德高将任意球吊入拥挤的禁区。一段头球混战后维拉解围。阿森纳的定位球还没有达到他们通常的标准。到目前为止。

bodyEn: Nothing ever remains the same. Entropy happens. Evolution happens. People grow, people shrink. The world changes and we must change with it. Change happens. The key is to keep ahead of that change, to guide it. The problem for Aston Villa this summer is that it has felt like change has been happening to them, the understandable desire to rejuvenate the squad coinciding with players being lured away by bigger salaries at more established clubs. The danger is of a vicious spiral, of the exodus inspiring further exodus as faith in the project is lost.

This, though, was a game to steady Villa nerves after the embarrassment at Brighton last Saturday – even if there had been a sense of pressure mounting uncomfortably before Bukayo Saka put Arsenal ahead. Villa might even have taken a first-half lead had Emí Buendia’s drive not come back off the bar. The champions were the better side, but there wasn’t a huge gulf between them. There was certainly enough here for Villa fans to believe that, even if this is a period of transition, the team they might turn into at the end of that process could be extremely useful.

The North Stand offers a visual representation of the state of change, the roof gone and the lower tier reduced to rows of concrete steps with a large bite taken out in either corner. A big hole has gone from the middle of the upper tier as well, offering a view through to the concrete struts beneath. Floodlighting is provided by two flimsy‑looking temporary towers. It’s all a bit ramshackle and patched together. But in time the old 6,000 structure will become a modern stand holding 12,000, as capacity climbs to almost 50,000 in time for Euro 2028. After a fallow season, it will return bigger and better than before, but there is an unavoidable period of rebuilding.

If all goes well, the same is true of the squad. Nine players have left, most notably Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Emí Martínez and Ezri Konsa, who came on to make his Arsenal debut, with the enormously promising Senegalese 18-year-old forward Ibrahim Mbaye and the 24-year-old centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis poised to become the eighth and ninth permanent arrivals on Tuesday.

Two players, the goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and the centre-forward Nicolas Jackson, made their first starts for the club. Suzuki’s performance was mixed. He misjudged one early corner and a late drive bounced off his chest with an alarming thump – gaffs such as that were a feature of his time at Parma, but the Japan goalkeeper still impressed, less in any specific save than with the authority of his demeanour. A large part of goalkeeping, like refereeing and management, is looking the part, persuading others to believe in you.

Suzuki also played a couple of remarkable long passes. One 60‑yard drive hit to George Hemmings with a touch of fade was so well calibrated that the young winger could take it on his shoulder on the move, and drew appreciative gasps from those in the Holte End directly behind the line of the pass.

Jackson was involved only intermittently but he gave some indication of what he might be capable of just before half-time, dispossessing Gabriel, surging 60 yards and then almost picking out Hemmings in the middle with a cleverly shaped cross. He always seemed a little unfortunate at Chelsea, plucked from Villarreal after 16 first-team appearances and expected to lead the line for a Premier League club that was in perpetual turmoil. His movement and capacity to run in behind defences has never been in doubt; where he struggled was in his decision-making. It may be that with maturity and in a side as structured as Villa that aspect of his game improves.

Matteo Ruggeri, Aaron Wan‑Bissaka and the loan signing Alejandro Garnacho were named on the bench, while Leon Goretzka isn’t even at that stage. Wan-Bissaka and Garnacho came on with 12 minutes to go, a debut for the full-back and a second substitute appearance for the winger. Piece by painstaking piece, a second Emery Villa is beginning to take shape.

It will, though, clearly be a significant time before every new signing is assimilated. There are a lot of new components to get used to Emery’s marathon video sessions and fit together. Villa began last season with a run of six games without a win and this season has the potential to be similarly tricky. It may be a season of hoping the European campaign goes well enough that they’re still involved come the spring and then, if Emery’s new side has come together, focusing on the Champions League knockouts and possibly a late surge to qualify for the competition next season.

The new Villa will not be built overnight, and successive defeats without scoring a goal obviously do not represent a great start. There will have to be patience. But the vaguest hints of a new side are beginning to emerge.
items.author: Jonathan Wilson at Villa Park
items.titleZh: 埃梅里的新球队开始成形，阿斯顿维拉在场内外重建 | 乔纳森·威尔逊
items.summaryZh: 尽管被击败，但这场对阵阿森纳的比赛在夏季动荡后稳定了球队的神经。
bodyZh: 没有什么是一成不变的。熵在发生，进化在发生。人在成长，也在衰变。世界在变，我们必须随之改变。变化总会发生，关键是保持领先于变化，引导变化。阿斯顿维拉今年夏天的问题在于，感觉变化正在发生在他们身上：重建阵容的愿望可以理解，但同时也伴随着球员被更大俱乐部的高薪所诱惑而离队。危险在于恶性循环，随着对项目的信心丧失，流失引发更多流失。
不过，这场比赛足以让维拉在上周六输给布莱顿的尴尬之后稳住心神——即使布卡约·萨卡为阿森纳取得领先之前，压力已经令人不安地累积。如果埃米·布恩迪亚的劲射没有击中横梁，维拉甚至可能在上半场取得领先。冠军球队是更好的一方，但双方差距并不悬殊。这里展现的内容足以让维拉球迷相信，即使这是一个过渡期，这个过程结束时他们可能成为的球队会非常有竞争力。
北看台直观地展示了变化的状态：屋顶没了，下层看台变成了几排混凝土台阶，两角各被咬掉一大块。上层看台中间也有一个大洞，可以看到下面的混凝土支柱。照明由两座看起来很简陋的临时塔架提供。这里一切都有些破旧和拼凑。但假以时日，这个拥有6000个座位的老结构将变成一个容纳12000人的现代看台，容量将在2028年欧洲杯前攀升至近50000人。经过一个荒芜的赛季后，它将比以前更大更好，但重建时期不可避免。
如果一切顺利，阵容也将如此。已有九名球员离队，最著名的是摩根·罗杰斯、尤里·蒂勒曼斯、埃米·马丁内斯和埃兹里·孔萨，后者替补登场完成了阿森纳首秀。极有前途的塞内加尔18岁前锋易卜拉欣·姆巴耶和24岁中后卫泰勒·哈伍德-贝利斯有望在周二成为第八和第九位永久加盟的球员。
两名球员——门将铃木彩太和中锋尼古拉斯·杰克逊——首次代表球队首发。铃木的表现喜忧参半。他一次早期角球判断失误，一次后期射门砰地一声击中胸口，令人惊恐——这类失误是他效力帕尔马时期的特点，但这位日本门将仍然令人印象深刻，与其说是具体的扑救，不如说是他神态中的威严。守门员的很大一部分，就像裁判和管理者一样，是要看起来像那么回事，说服别人相信你。
铃木还送出了几脚出色的长传。一次60码的传球给到乔治·海明斯，带着内旋，校准得如此精准，以至于这位年轻边锋可以在移动中用肩膀卸下，引得传球线路正后方的霍尔特看台观众发出赞叹。
杰克逊只是间歇性参与，但他在半场结束前展现了一些潜力：抢断加布里埃尔，推进60码，然后用一记巧妙弧线的传中几乎找到中路的海明斯。他在切尔西时总显得有些不幸，在比利亚雷亚尔只出场16次一线队比赛就被挖走，并被期望为一家长期动荡的英超俱乐部领导锋线。他的跑动和插入防线身后的能力从未被质疑；他挣扎的地方在于决策。随着成熟，以及在像维拉这样有结构的球队中，他的这一方面可能会提高。
马泰奥·鲁杰里、亚伦·万-比萨卡和租借加盟的亚历杭德罗·加纳乔被列入了替补名单，而莱昂·格雷茨卡甚至还没有达到这一步。万-比萨卡和加纳乔在还剩12分钟时替补登场，这是边后卫的首秀，也是边锋的第二次替补出场。一块一块地拼凑，第二个埃梅里时代的维拉开始成形。

不过，显然还需要相当长的时间才能让所有新援融入。有很多新部件需要适应埃梅里马拉松式的视频会议并整合起来。维拉上赛季以六场不胜开局，本赛季也有可能同样棘手。这可能是一个希望欧战表现足够好、能坚持到春季的赛季，然后，如果埃梅里的新球队已经成形，再专注于欧冠淘汰赛，并可能为下赛季的参赛资格发起冲刺。
新的维拉不会一夜建成，连续失利且一球未进显然不是一个好的开局。必须有耐心。但一支全新球队的最模糊迹象已经开始显现。

bodyEn: The smile on Declan Rice’s face with six minutes of normal time remaining said it all. He had just shut down Ian Maatsen as the Aston Villa full-back zoomed into the box. Arsenal, for whom Bukayo Saka scored the only goal, were authoritative and seemingly took great satisfaction in keeping Villa at arm’s length.

Unai Emery’s work‑in‑progress side struggled to test the champions, David Raya untroubled. The records will show Villa have lost their first two league matches of a season without scoring for the first time since 2002 but, despite successive defeats, this time there was no capitulation.
For Villa, this was a marked improvement on defeat at Brighton in their opener. After 31 minutes in their previous game, they trailed 4-0 and after 40 were down to 10 men.

Here they could take plenty of encouragement from a promising if not fruitless performance, the debutants Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson impressing, having taken the No 1 and No 11 shirts vacated by Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins respectively. Suzuki and Jackson were the only changes to Villa’s starting XI but they appeared far more cohesive. Suzuki’s eye for a pass was particularly noticeable, pinging 50-yard passes to George Hemmings, the 19-year-old who kept his place, and John McGinn within a few minutes of each other.

Emi Buendía smacked the crossbar after Boubacar Kamara overawed Christos Tzolis – Martin Ødegaard subsequently asked questions of the referee, Jarred Gillett – but Jackson otherwise created Villa’s best opening. The Senegal forward, who worked under Emery at Villarreal, pinched possession from Gabriel Magalhães a few yards into the Villa half and galloped into the other before sending a near-perfect cross in from the right. Hemmings burst into the six-yard box but was unable to convert. Villa are just the second team to fail to register a shot on target in their first two Premier League matches in a season since 2003-04, along with Swansea City in 2017-18.

This fixture last season ended in despair for Arsenal, their players splayed across the turf after Buendía’s 95th-minute winner with the last kick of the game. Arteta said that defeat still haunts him and reminded his players as much before this game. “That was still in my tummy and I spoke to my players about it, the image of the players on the floor, totally gutted,” the Arsenal manager said. “We used that [as inspiration].”

In that game last season Eberechi Eze was at fault for Matty Cash’s opener and was subsequently hooked at half-time. Here it was a case of role‑reversal, Eze shining after coming on for the second half in place of Christos Tzolis, who was booked after a foul on Cash and muted.

“I think he learnt a lesson,” Arteta said of Eze, who was involved in Arsenal seizing the lead approaching the hour. Arsenal slowed things down and then punished Villa for switching off. Cristhian Mosquera pushed a pass to Eze, who was afforded space by Cash, Villa’s defender concerned about an unmarked Riccardo Calafiori. Eze promptly spied Calafiori’s underlapping run and the Italian steered the ball across the six-yard box where Saka beat Maatsen to the punch and scrambled the cross into the net.

This is a new-look Villa, on and off the pitch. A handful of staff in hard hats were positioned in the closed North Stand moonlighting as ball boys; the corner of rubble between the remaining skeleton and the Trinity Road Stand remains akin to an excavation site. Ibrahim Mbaye, whose £47m move from Paris Saint‑Germain is to be announced on Tuesday, was in the directors’ box. Taylor Harwood-Bellis is also poised to sign in a £25m deal from Southampton. Six of Villa’s starting XI from their Europa League triumph may have departed but Emery has made no complaints and has relayed his no-excuses mantra to his squad. “We do not look backwards,” he said.

Villa’s frustrations were palpable. McGinn, in a hurry to get Villa level, was booked for wiping out Merino. Aaron Wan-Bissaka replaced Cash for his Villa debut and his first job was to stretch his legs to muffle an advancing Eze. Alejandro Garnacho entered in place of Ross Barkley. Arteta introduced Ezri Konsa for his debut, adding further steel.
Villa could not find a way through and Arsenal’s winning habit already appears ominous. “It is painful to lose,” Emery said. “But we can feel optimistic with how we competed.”

items.titleZh: 萨卡制胜，阿森纳力克维拉延续开局连胜
items.summaryZh: 萨卡制胜，阿森纳力克维拉延续连胜。维拉两连败且未进球。
bodyZh: 常规时间还剩六分钟时，德克兰·赖斯脸上的笑容说明了一切。他刚刚在阿斯顿维拉边后卫伊恩·马特森突入禁区时将其封堵。阿森纳凭借布卡约·萨卡的唯一进球，表现得非常稳健，似乎对让维拉无法靠近球门感到十分满意。
乌奈·埃梅里仍在打造中的球队难以考验冠军，大卫·拉亚没有受到什么威胁。记录显示，维拉自2002年以来首次在赛季前两场联赛中均失利且未进球，但尽管遭遇连败，这一次他们没有崩溃。
对维拉而言，这比首轮输给布莱顿时有明显改善。上一场比赛中，他们在第31分钟就以0-4落后，第40分钟更是少一人作战。
在这里，他们可以从一场有希望且并非徒劳的表现中获得大量鼓励，首秀的铃木彩艳和尼古拉斯·杰克逊给人留下深刻印象，他们分别接过了埃米利亚诺·马丁内斯和奥利·沃特金斯留下的1号和11号球衣。铃木和杰克逊是维拉首发阵容中仅有的变化，但他们看起来更加协调。铃木的传球视野尤其引人注目，他在几分钟内分别向19岁的乔治·赫明斯（后者保住了位置）和约翰·麦金送出50码的长传。

埃米·布恩迪亚在布巴卡尔·卡马拉压制了克里斯托斯·佐利斯后大力射门击中横梁——随后马丁·厄德高向裁判贾里德·吉莱特提出了质疑——但除此之外，杰克逊创造了维拉最好的机会。这位塞内加尔前锋曾在比利亚雷亚尔与埃梅里共事，他在维拉半场距几码处从加布里埃尔·马加良斯脚下滑铲夺球，然后快速突入另一侧，从右路送出一记近乎完美的传中。赫明斯冲入六码区但未能将球打进。维拉成为继2017-18赛季的斯旺西城之后，自2003-04赛季以来第二支在赛季前两场英超比赛中没有一次射正球门的球队。
上赛季的这场比赛以阿森纳的绝望告终，布恩迪亚在第95分钟用比赛的最后一脚完成绝杀，阿森纳球员瘫倒在草坪上。阿尔特塔表示，那场失利至今仍让他耿耿于怀，并在本场比赛前提醒了他的球员。“那场失利仍在我的心头，我和球员们谈过这件事，球员们瘫倒在地的画面，完全心碎。”阿森纳主帅说，“我们以此作为激励。”
在上赛季的那场比赛中，埃贝雷基·埃泽对马蒂·卡什的首开纪录负有责任，随后在中场时被替换下场。这次则出现了角色互换，埃泽在下半场替补克里斯托斯·佐利斯出场后表现出色，而佐利斯则因对卡什犯规被黄牌警告并表现平平。
“我认为他吸取了教训，”阿尔特塔谈到埃泽时说，后者在阿森纳临近第60分钟时取得领先的过程中发挥了作用。阿森纳放慢了节奏，然后惩罚了走神的维拉。克里斯蒂安·莫斯克拉将球传给埃泽，埃泽得到了卡什给予的空间，维拉后卫担心无人盯防的里卡尔多·卡拉菲奥里。埃泽立即看到了卡拉菲奥里的底线套边跑动，后者将球横穿六码区，萨卡比马特森抢先一步，将球捅入网窝。

这是一支全新面貌的维拉，无论是在场上还是场下。几名戴安全帽的工作人员站在封闭的北看台上客串球童；残存骨架与特里尼蒂路看台之间的碎石角落仍像是一个考古挖掘现场。易卜拉欣·姆巴耶，这位以4700万英镑从巴黎圣日耳曼转会而来的球员将于周二官宣，他坐在董事包厢里。泰勒·哈伍德-贝利斯也准备以2500万英镑从南安普顿签下。维拉欧联杯夺冠阵容中的六名首发可能已经离开，但埃梅里没有抱怨，并将“没有借口”的理念传达给了球队。“我们不回顾过去，”他说。
维拉的沮丧是显而易见的。麦金急于为维拉扳平比分，因放倒梅里诺而被黄牌警告。亚伦·万-比萨卡换下卡什完成维拉首秀，他的第一项任务就是伸长腿限制埃泽的推进。亚历杭德罗·加纳乔换下罗斯·巴克利。阿尔特塔则让埃兹里·孔萨上演首秀，进一步加强了防守。
维拉找不到突破口，而阿森纳的赢球习惯似乎已经显现出威胁。“输球很痛苦，”埃梅里说，“但我们可以对竞争的方式感到乐观。”

bodyEn: Arsenal have asked the Premier League to increase the size of matchday squads, with Mikel Arteta saying the current system is detrimental to player welfare. Top‑flight clubs can name 20 players for games, including a minimum of three homegrown players. In Spain’s La Liga, clubs can name a matchday squad of 23, while Italy’s Serie A allows 25.

Arsenal have competed on multiple fronts in recent seasons. Last year, as well as winning the Premier League, they reached the finals of the Champions League and Carabao Cup, as well as the quarter-finals of the FA Cup. With pressure increasing on the football calendar and players facing more matches, Arteta sees no reason why English teams should operate with smaller squads than those from other European leagues.

“I’ve been begging the Premier League if we can extend those numbers just for the welfare of the players, which is the most important thing, because I think every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demand in international games that we have,” Arteta said, as he prepares for the champions’ trip to Aston Villa on Monday night. “But these are the rules, and within the rules we have to play. We need to be very close to the players to explain those situations in the right way, for everybody to feel important, because they will be.”

Clubs can register a squad of 25 senior players – those aged over 21 – for the season, with at least eight homegrown. As a result, five senior players registered for the season miss out each game. Arteta has said it can be difficult to tell players they are not involved and that the news can negatively affect their wellbeing.

“The question has to be to the players. What do they want? If they raise their hands and say: ‘No, I prefer to stay at home and not travel,’ I think we have an issue because then they don’t love what they do, which is the matchday,” he said. “But I’m sure that if you ask the players, everybody would like to be part of the squad on matchday, because that’s the way that they can fulfil themselves.

“Otherwise you have to tell somebody: ‘You are not even part of this matchday,’ and that’s really tough. And it doesn’t help anybody. It doesn’t help the club. It doesn’t help the valuation of the player. It doesn’t help the player feel part of something. It’s a real issue that has a really simple solution.”

Arteta added: “And all the clubs, because I’ve done the research with all the top clubs in Europe, we are not different to anybody. Most of them, 90% of them, they have more players than us. So we are going to have to deal with that.”

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔“恳求”英超扩大20人比赛日大名单
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳主帅称弃用球员影响健康，意甲和西甲可报名25人和23人。
bodyZh: 阿森纳已要求英超联赛扩大比赛日大名单规模，米克尔·阿尔特塔表示现行制度不利于球员福祉。英超俱乐部每场比赛可报名20名球员，其中至少包括3名本土培养球员。而西班牙的西甲允许报名23人，意大利的意甲则允许25人。
阿森纳近几个赛季多线作战。去年，他们不仅赢得了英超冠军，还闯入了欧冠和联赛杯决赛，以及足总杯四分之一决赛。随着足球赛程压力增大，球员面临更多比赛，阿尔特塔认为英格兰球队没有理由以比欧洲其他联赛更小的阵容规模运作。
“我一直在恳求英超联赛，为了球员的福祉——这是最重要的事情——能否扩大这些数字，因为我认为每支球队理想情况下需要的场上球员超过20人，才能应对我们所面临的国际比赛需求，”阿尔特塔在为冠军球队周一晚客场挑战阿斯顿维拉做准备时表示。“但规则就是这样，我们必须在规则范围内比赛。我们需要与球员保持密切沟通，以恰当的方式解释这些情况，让每个人都感到被重视，因为他们确实重要。”
俱乐部每个赛季可注册25名资深球员（年龄超过21岁）的大名单，其中至少8名为本土培养。因此，每场比赛会有5名注册的资深球员落选。阿尔特塔表示，告诉球员他们无法出战可能很困难，这一消息会对他们的心理健康产生负面影响。
“问题应该抛给球员。他们想要什么？如果他们举手说：‘不，我宁愿待在家里不随队旅行。’我想那就有问题了，因为那样他们就不热爱自己做的事，也就是比赛日，”他说。“但我敢肯定，如果你问球员们，每个人都希望成为比赛日大名单的一员，因为那是他们实现自我价值的方式。”
“否则你就得告诉某个人：‘你连这次比赛日大名单都没进。’那真的很残酷，对任何人都没有帮助。对俱乐部没帮助，对球员的估值没帮助，也无法让球员感受到归属感。这是一个真正的问题，但解决方案却很简单。”
阿尔特塔补充道：“而且所有俱乐部——因为我做过欧洲所有顶级俱乐部的研究——我们并不比别人特殊。他们大多数，90%的俱乐部，球员都比我们多。所以我们必须面对这一点。”

bodyEn: The 36 clubs in the Champions League know who they will play in the league phase, but which team has the kindest draw and who has the toughest assignment? Each side knows their eight opponents, but, given no two teams face the same set of opponents, this is not a level playing field. We have used the Opta power rankings – which rank 16,000 teams from across the world on the same scale – to find out who did best in the draw.
Who have the English clubs got?

Arsenal: Napoli (a), 9 September; Lille (h), 13 October; Bayern Munich (a), 21 October; Slavia Prague (a), 4 November; Borussia Dortmund (h), 24 November; Real Madrid (h), 9 December; Real Betis (a), 20 January; Sabah (h), 27 January
